root_cause.text: `btusb_probe()` allocated the shared `struct btusb_data` with `devm_kzalloc()` on one USB interface, so `btusb_disconnect()` could trigger automatic freeing of state still referenced by other btusb-bound interfaces (`ISOC`/`DIAG`), causing a use-after-free/race due to mismatched object lifetime management in `drivers/bluetooth/btusb.c`.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE text says `devm_kzalloc()` “ties the lifetime of all the btusb data to the binding of a driver to one interface, INTF” and that in `btusb_disconnect()`, `usb_driver_release_interface(&btusb_driver, data->intf)` “will have devm free the data that is also being used by the other interfaces”; the patch fixes this by replacing `devm_kzalloc(&intf->dev, ...)` with `kzalloc(...)` and adding explicit `kfree(data)` in error and disconnect paths.

intent_record.intent_summary: Switch btusb_probe() to manually allocated memory for 'data' instead of devm-managed allocation.
intent_record.what: In btusb_probe(), the allocation for 'data' was changed from devm_kzalloc(&intf->dev, sizeof(*data), GFP_KERNEL) to kzalloc(sizeof(*data), GFP_KERNEL); the surrounding NULL check and -ENOMEM return remain unchanged.
intent_record.how: This changes the allocation from device-managed memory to manually managed heap memory, so the object will no longer be automatically freed when the device is detached; lifetime management must now be handled elsewhere to avoid leaks or use-after-free issues.

intent_record.intent_summary: Free the allocated driver data when required USB endpoints are missing during btusb probe.
intent_record.what: The probe function now wraps the endpoint presence check in braces and adds a call to kfree(data) before returning -ENODEV when any of intr_ep, bulk_tx_ep, or bulk_rx_ep is missing.
intent_record.how: If the Bluetooth USB device does not provide the required endpoints, the driver now releases the allocated btusb data structure before failing probe, preventing a memory leak on this error path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Free the probe data when HCI device allocation fails to prevent a memory leak.
intent_record.what: In btusb_probe(), the failure path after hci_alloc_dev_priv(priv_size) was changed from a bare null check returning -ENOMEM to a braced block that first calls kfree(data) and then returns -ENOMEM.
intent_record.how: If HCI device allocation fails during USB Bluetooth device probing, the previously allocated data structure is now freed before exiting, preventing a memory leak on the error path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Free btusb private data on probe failure to fix a memory leak.
intent_record.what: A call to kfree(data) was added just before returning from btusb_probe() after hci_free_dev(hdev), following the existing reset GPIO cleanup.
intent_record.how: If btusb_probe() exits through this error path, the btusb private data structure is now released instead of being left allocated, preventing a memory leak during probe failure cleanup.

intent_record.intent_summary: Free the btusb device निजी data on disconnect to fix a memory leak.
intent_record.what: In `btusb_disconnect(struct usb_interface *intf)`, a new call to `kfree(data);` was added immediately after `hci_free_dev(hdev);`.
intent_record.how: When the Bluetooth USB device is disconnected, the driver now frees the `data` allocation associated with the device after releasing the HCI device, preventing that memory from remaining allocated after disconnect.

consistency_review.core_intent: Free btusb private data on probe failure to fix a memory leak.

relevance_review.reason: The change switches btusb_probe() away from devm-managed allocation to manual allocation and adds explicit freeing on failure, which directly addresses the root cause of incorrect lifetime management of shared btusb_data that could otherwise be freed too early and cause a use-after-free.

The change only adds cleanup on HCI device allocation failure to prevent a leak. It does not address the root cause of the use-after-free from devm-managed btusb_data being freed while other interfaces still reference it.

The group changes btusb disconnect-time freeing of device private data, which is directly tied to the shared btusb_data lifetime issue described in the root cause. Even though the stated intent is to fix a leak, it targets the same object-lifetime management in btusb_disconnect() that caused the use-after-free/race.

candidates.rationale: This allocates the shared btusb private state with device-managed lifetime on a single USB interface, which can be freed automatically when that interface disconnects even though other btusb-bound interfaces still reference it, creating the use-after-free/race described in the root cause.

vuln_statements.explanation: This line allocates the shared btusb private state with device-managed lifetime on a single USB interface, so disconnecting that interface can free the object while other btusb-bound interfaces still hold references, causing the use-after-free/race.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet clearly shows the vulnerable lifetime change: in `btusb_probe()` the shared device state is allocated with `data = devm_kzalloc(&intf->dev, sizeof(*data), GFP_KERNEL);` instead of plain `kzalloc()`. This is the exact construct tied to the root cause, because the `struct btusb_data` lifetime becomes managed by the USB interface device and can be freed automatically when one interface disconnects. The code still shares `data` across other btusb-bound interfaces, as indicated by references such as `data->isoc` and `usb_driver_release_interface(&btusb_driver, data->isoc);` in `btusb_disconnect()`, but there is no fix here to prevent premature release or to manage a shared refcounted lifetime. The explicit `kfree(data);` removals in probe and disconnect show the commit intentionally switched to devm-managed allocation rather than correcting the shared-object lifetime issue, so the vulnerable construct is present and the fix is not present in this version.
